# One product, scenario-aware posters

- Walk-in, including Founders, is one product with one feature set and one shared poster system. Hackathon entries change the presentation, not the available features or implementation.
- Adapt the poster to the scenario: a business launch, a Founders campaign, or a location-focused invitation. Support campaigns started with or without a survey.
- Design for the particular business, not a generic template with its name swapped in. Use its actual concept, offer, audience and visual identity to shape the composition, typography, palette and original visual motif. Changing colors alone is not enough.
- Lead with what attracts a customer: what this business offers and why someone would visit. Survey scores, catchment analysis and internal planning labels are not the advertising message.
- For Founders, prominently show the real participation perks and who receives them. A pledge amount or funding goal is not a substitute for explaining the benefit.
- Never invent a perk, discount, price, opening date, capacity or guarantee. Use the owner's approved terms and campaign data.
- Assess a map by its value to the customer. Do not reserve a large map area or shrink the business offer and perks just to preserve a decorative survey map. If retained, make it genuinely useful for finding the business.
- Use only artwork and brand assets the owner has rights to use. Do not copy another business's poster or imply endorsements from artists, shows or brands in the taste data.
- Give the QR code a clear action and useful destination: the campaign or the owner's approved page. Never print a private receipt link. Keep a readable link and appropriate print contrast and QR quiet space.
- Use brand-appropriate palettes and subtle background or cast-shadow motifs that relate to the business. Keep artwork clear of important text.
- A decorative QR frame must stay outside the white quiet zone; do not color, blur, distort or cover QR modules. Verify exact destinations from exported PNGs and printed PDFs, not only the screen preview.
- Keep payment conditions and sandbox disclosures accurate and legible, without letting them replace the offer or perks.
- Review different businesses side by side before calling the design finished. They should feel intentionally designed for different projects, and screen, print and download outputs must agree.
